slides.title: RAII Locking Mechanics
slides.prompt: To prevent dangling locks when exceptions occur or code exits early, C++ uses RAII wrappers. std::lock_guard provides lightweight scope-based locking, while std::unique_lock adds flexibility like deferred locking and explicit manual locking/unlocking.

slides.title: std::lock_guard Usage
slides.prompt: Fill in the class template used for simple scope-bound lock acquisition.

slides.title: std::lock_guard vs std::unique_lock
slides.prompt: What is a key capability of std::unique_lock that std::lock_guard lacks?
options: std::unique_lock can be unlocked manually before exiting scope and supports condition variables
std::unique_lock is lighter and faster than lock_guard
std::unique_lock supports copy operations across threads
std::unique_lock does not require a mutex reference
slides.correctAnswer: std::unique_lock can be unlocked manually before exiting scope and supports condition variables

slides.title: Deferred Locking Flag
slides.prompt: Fill in the lock tag used with std::unique_lock to construct the wrapper without acquiring the lock immediately.

slides.title: Adopt Lock Tag
slides.prompt: What does the tag std::adopt_lock indicate when passed to a lock guard or unique_lock constructor?
options: The calling thread already owns the lock on the mutex, so do not lock it again
Adopt lock ownership from another thread
Lock the mutex immediately using try_lock
Create a copy of an existing lock
slides.correctAnswer: The calling thread already owns the lock on the mutex, so do not lock it again

slides.title: C++17 std::scoped_lock
slides.prompt: Fill in the C++17 lock wrapper designed to safely lock multiple mutexes simultaneously without deadlocks.
slides.codeSnippet:
std::mutex m1, m2;
std::___ lock(m1, m2); // Locks both m1 and m2 deadlock-free

slides.title: std::shared_lock for Readers
slides.prompt: Which lock wrapper works with std::shared_mutex to acquire a shared (read-only) lock?

slides.title: Transferring Lock Ownership
slides.prompt: Fill in the standard operation used to transfer ownership of a std::unique_lock to another function.

slides.title: Copyability of RAII Locks
options: Neither is copyable; unique_lock is move-only, while lock_guard is neither copyable nor movable
Both are fully copyable and movable
lock_guard is copyable, unique_lock is move-only
Both are movable but not copyable
slides.correctAnswer: Neither is copyable; unique_lock is move-only, while lock_guard is neither copyable nor movable
